title: Choose Saga’s visual world
question: The proposed direction makes dependencies the organizing structure. Keep it, choose an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Signal Box
options.lineage: railway interlocking diagrams and dispatch boards
options.thesis: Saga becomes a live dispatch surface where every task occupies a block and every dependency controls the signal ahead.
options.viewport: A compact ledger sits beside a wide dependency route: status signals, junctions, and task blocks reveal what can move next.
options.risk: The route metaphor must remain subordinate to task names and familiar filtering controls.

options.label: Phosphor Terminal
options.lineage: green-phosphor terminals in a midnight machine room
options.thesis: The dashboard reads as one searchable machine transcript with task state printed directly into the flow.
options.case: Strong developer recognition, but weaker spatial clarity for hierarchy and converging dependencies.
options.viewport: An 80-column task index and selected-task transcript fill the screen with no detached chrome.
options.risk: Long sessions and graph tracing suffer if terminal theater overpowers information density.

options.label: One-bit Desktop
options.thesis: Hierarchy, graph, and detail appear as crisp overlapping tools on a black-and-white project desktop.
options.case: Excellent operational clarity and compact controls, though nostalgia may distract from Saga’s current workflow.
options.viewport: A task window, dependency-map window, and inspector tile into a dense monochrome workspace.
options.risk: Pixel grammar can become costume unless every interaction behaves consistently.

options.label: Deployable Sheet
options.thesis: Task groups unfold from compact packets into a linked crease field where one state change propagates visibly.
options.case: Dependency propagation is memorable, but the unfamiliar folding model increases interpretation cost.
options.viewport: Summary packets open into a diagonal task field while the complete dependency graph remains inspectable.
options.risk: Diagonal geometry could compromise title scanning and responsive layout.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A polished neutral task dashboard with summary cards, filters, a board, and a conventional node graph.
canonCard.viewport: Metrics lead into a familiar task table with the dependency graph in a secondary tab.
canonCard.risk: Easy to learn, but it makes Saga look interchangeable with generic project software.
